activityGoals.name: Updating an Element in the Array (Case 1)
activityGoals.goalDescription: Construct a program that initializes an array with three integers, changes the first element in the array, and finally, prints all the array elements.

lineList.content: //#Step 1: Define an array of three integers

commentList: We want to assign three integers to the array. Therefore, we need to define the array of type int. In this statement, we declare and initialize the array values with three integers. We initialize the array by separating elements with a comma and enclosing the collection in braces { }.
This statement updates the first element of the array to value 2 (int data type).

To update an element in the array, we need to give the square bracket slice operator ([ ] ) along with an index of the element that we want to update on the left-hand side of the assignment operator. The index could start at 0 and continue up to but not including the length of the array. The value on the right-hand side of the assignment operator is the new value that we want to assign to the array element.

To print the array elements, we need to traverse the array and then print each element as we visit it. We traverse the array elements using for–each statement. This for loop assigns the name x to each of the elements in the array in turn, from left to right, and the print statement will be executed for each.
This statement prints the element that we visited in the array followed by a space character.

Note that we don't use println because it adds an end-of-line character to terminate the output line. We want to print all the elements of the array in the same line; therefore, we use the print method.
